title: vectorized-dequant-fusion-and-kv-alignment-batcher
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: production workloads saw uneven gains from the INT8/FP8 serving paths due to two related problems: 1) dequantization happening as a separate op after KV cache materialization created memory traffic and prevented kernel fusion, and 2) scheduling decisions did not account for quantization alignment in the KV cache which caused small but frequent parity fallbacks to FP16 that kill tail latency.

This PR introduces a new vectorized dequant-fusion operator and scheduler hints to: (a) consume quantized KV cache entries in-place, apply per-head smoothing/scale adjustments (smoothquant-inspired), and emit requantized activations fused with the attention microkernel; (b) align continuous batching decisions to prefer grouping requests with compatible quant metadata (scale/zero point/signature) so kernels can be reused across microbatches; (c) add a conservative FP8 compatibility check and graceful fallback threshold to avoid correctness regressions.

High level changes: new native kernels (C++/CUDA) for fused vectorized dequant+requant, scheduler heuristics in the runtime planner, KV cache metadata extension (small 16B signature per cache entry), continuous-batcher grouping changes, benchmark harness updates, and unit+integration tests.

Checklist:
- [x] microkernel implementation and CPU fallback
- [x] runtime scheduler integration and policy flag (runtime.quant_kv_alignment=true)
- [x] perf benches (see commits)
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] canary perf rollout config
- [x] docs note in optimization guide

Related: ENG-14234 (quant roadmap), SUP-7321 (customer incident describing FP16 fallbacks)
commits_summary: 1) add vectorized vdequant kernel and CUDA implementation; 2) runtime: KV cache metadata signature + alignment hints; 3) batcher: group by quant-signature and seq-length bucket; 4) attention kernel: hook fused requant path; 5) tests and benchmarks; 6) docs: optimization guide entry; 7) small perf fixes after review (locking and atomic counters)
files_changed_summary: src/runtime/scheduler/planner.cc (heuristics for quant alignment), src/runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache.rs (signature attach/read), src/kernels/cuda/vdequant.cu (new fused kernel), src/kernels/cpu/vdequant.cc (fallback), src/kernels/attention/attn_fused.cu (hooked requant path), python/benchmarks/quant_benchmarks.py (added int8/seq buckets), tests/integration/test_quant_kv_alignment.py, docs/optimizations/quantization.md, tools/canary/configs/quant_kv_rollout.yaml
review_thread:
Marco: Can you share numbers for seq_len=1024 and batch sizes 1/4/8 on A100? Also how does this behave for causal vs non-causal attention?
Aisha: Benchmarks attached; see ci artifact perf/quant-bench-20250212.csv. For causal attention we reuse the same fused path; non-causal saw ~3% extra memory traffic due to padding but still benefits.
Samantha: Is the KV signature guaranteed stable across model sharding and checkpoint loading? Potential mismatch could cause silent correctness issues.
Aisha: KV signature is derived from the model-scale vector and quant config saved into the checkpoint header; added tests to validate reload and mismatch triggers conservative FP16 fallback.
Ethan: CI regression on nightly showed a nondeterministic failure in test_quant_kv_alignment on CPU fallback; reproducer?
Aisha: Found a race in the cache GC path exposed by the new metadata access, fixed with a lightweight RCU guard and added deterministic ordering in test. Follow-up commit added.
Marco: Approving pending a small doc clarification on the rollout config and a canary window recommendation.
Aisha: Addressed docs, updated canary to 6-hour ramp and added metric dashboards (p50/p95/p99, fallback-rate). Marco: Approved. Samantha: Approved.
Merge: squashed after final CI pass.
ci_checks: perf-regression: pass (1.12x tokens/sec on int8, 14% p99 latency reduction)
merge_details: merged by Marco Ruiz (squash) on 2025-02-18. Merge commit message: 'vectorized dequant fusion + KV alignment batcher; improve INT8 throughput and reduce FP16 fallback rate. Resolves ENG-14234.'
release_notes:
- Added fused vectorized dequant->requant kernels to reduce memory traffic and enable kernel fusion for INT8/FP8 inference.
- Scheduler now groups microbatches by quantization signature to improve kernel reuse in continuous batching.
- KV cache metadata extended to carry a 16B quant signature to avoid incompatible cache reuse.
- Default rollout: feature runtime.quant_kv_alignment=true; conservative FP8 fallback remains enabled.
Impact: expected up to ~1.1-1.3x throughput on INT8 paths and 10–18% reduction in p99 latency for typical seq_len 512–2048 workloads.
